Data sources

Weather Pulse does not calculate the forecasts itself and has no weather model of its own. The site shows data from open sources, arranges it and adds an estimate of how far it can be trusted. This page describes where every number comes from.

The weather forecast

All forecasts (current weather, 7 and 16 days, hourly and 15-minute) come from Open-Meteo. Open-Meteo collects the output of the numerical models of national weather services and serves it through an API. The site asks for it in the default “best match” mode: for each place and hour Open-Meteo itself chooses or combines the most suitable models, for example ICON from the German service DWD, IFS from ECMWF, GFS from the American NOAA and models from Météo-France. Weather Pulse does not decide or show which exact model produced a given number.

The forecast is more reliable for the first days and only a rough guide after day 7, as with all models.

How certain is the forecast

On the weather forecast page, two more things under the temperatures show the uncertainty:

  • Range and reliability. The ICON ensemble (40 runs with slightly different starting conditions) from the Open-Meteo Ensemble API is used. The range shown lies between the 10th and 90th percentile of the runs, so 80% of the runs fall inside it. Reliability depends on how much they disagree: up to 2° spread in the maximum is “Reliable forecast”, up to 4° “Fairly reliable forecast”, more is “Uncertain forecast”. Days after day 7 are marked “Rough forecast”.
  • Model comparison. The “Compare weather models” table shows the maximum temperature and the rain for each day from three separate models: ECMWF IFS (Europe), ICON (Germany) and GFS (USA). If they differ a lot, the forecast is uncertain.

All sources

DataSource
Weather forecast, sunrise and sunsetOpen-Meteo Forecast API
Range and reliability (ICON ensemble)Open-Meteo Ensemble API
ECMWF, ICON, GFS comparisonOpen-Meteo Forecast API with a chosen model (ecmwf_ifs025, icon_seamless, gfs_seamless)
Monthly climate on the city pagesOpen-Meteo Historical Weather API: ERA5 reanalysis, averages for 2015–2024
Place searchOpen-Meteo Geocoding API, and for “current location” OpenStreetMap Nominatim
Geomagnetic storms, Kp index, solar windNOAA Space Weather Prediction Center
Public holidaysNager.Date
Maps (wind, rain, clouds, temperature)Windy
Moon phaseCalculated on the site from the mean lunar month (29.53 days) counted from a known new moon, with no request to an outside source. Good as a guide, not for astronomically exact moments.

Limitations

  • Weather Pulse is not an official weather service. For warnings of dangerous weather (storms, floods, heat) follow your national service.
  • The data comes from models with a grid of points, not from station measurements. In mountains, valleys and on the coast the real temperature and rain may differ from what is shown.
  • The climate of each city comes from the ERA5 reanalysis with a grid of about 10 km, so for mountain places it may differ from the measurements of a weather station.
  • Open-Meteo is a free service. If it cannot be reached, the site shows an error message, not old data.
